chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni.
That Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning the hashimah that it carries compensation of ten camels.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, the authority issuing the legal ruling
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the unit of compensation in this ruling
key_terms.الْهَاشِمَةِ: an injury that breaks the bone, especially in the head or face, in the context of diyah rulings

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for al-hashimah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding the indemnity for a specific type of head or facial injury known as al-hashimah. It establishes that the prescribed diyah for this injury is ten camels within the law of bodily injuries.
